messages:
tara: quick sync — proposing a compact "model_stamp" schema for rollout metadata. goal: minimal surface for serving/runtime to decide compatible variants and soft-fallbacks. thoughts?

kevin: looks useful. can you call out how this differs from current 'pin' model? main worry is migration complexity and stale leases.

tara: yeah, main differences: 1) model_stamp is immutable once issued (like a signed artifact id), 2) it carries a small compatibility vector instead of heavy TTL-based leases, 3) includes a soft 'sticky_release' annotation to express affinity without hard eviction. avoids global lease churn.

nina: new terms sound good. show the minimal example you have in mind?

tara: sure — rough sketch below:

```
{
  "model_id": "redwood/longform-7b",
  "stamp": "sha256:7a3f...",
  "epoch": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z",
  "compat_tags": ["tok-v1","attn-v2"],
  "sticky_release": {
    "owner": "team-chat",
    "mode": "soft",        // soft | hard
    "expires_at": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z",
    "reason": "canary:traffic-affinity"
  },
  "canary_policy": "pct:5,duration:2h"
}
```

kevin: that helps. couple notes: we should avoid nested objects in the main runtime header to keep lookup cheap. maybe flatten sticky_release.* into fields prefixed like sticky_owner, sticky_mode, sticky_expires. cheaper for indexers.

nina: yes flattening makes sense. also: compat_tags should be small and normative (not free-form). we should enumerate accepted tag families (tokenizer, attention, kernel) and keep versions like tok:v1.

tara: agreed. proposal: keep a tiny header for runtime (flat) and allow an optional richer metadata blob for console/infra. runtime-visible fields: model_id, stamp, epoch, compat_tag_list (comma sep), sticky_owner, sticky_mode, sticky_expires, canary_pct, canary_window. all other fields live in metadata_blob which is opaque to runtime.

ryan: migration plan question: how do we map existing pins/leases? we have hundreds of tenant pins with TTLs. can't force all customers to repin.

tara: plan: 1) backfill a model_stamp for current pinned versions (stamp=content-hash, epoch=now), 2) translate TTL->sticky_expires for soft pins, 3) for leases that were hard pins we set sticky_mode=hard and keep legacy lease entry for 30 days as fallback. we'll run a backfill job and emit metrics.

kevin: make sure rollout evaluation uses both stamp equality and compat_tags subset match. we need deterministic fallback order: exact stamp -> same model_id + compat superset -> nearest semantic minor -> global fallback pool. document it.

nina: also add a 'regen_policy' field for automated repinning if weight drops too low (e.g., autoconvert to newer minor after N days). can be optional.

infra-bot: note: created ticket INFRA-2385 to add flat index fields and start backfill. Estimated run time: 6h for prod index.

ryan: UX: console should show both runtime_header and metadata_blob. console teams asked for reasons and owner links. keep metadata blob JSON for that.

tara: decision checklist I'm capturing:
- runtime header flat fields only (yes)
- compat tag family enum (yes)
- migration/backfill plan (yes, INFRA-2385)
- canary policy tokens (pct + duration) (yes)
- soft vs hard sticky semantics + 30d legacy fallback (yes)

kevin: fine from infra side. please add explicit TTL->sticky_expires mapping rules in the ticket before backfill.

nina: I'll draft the compat tag families and a small doc for model-onboarding checklist.

tara: thanks. if nobody objects I'll post an RFC summary and assign owners for PRs (index + backfill + console) tomorrow. :thumbsup:

kevin: no objections. :+1:

ryan: LGTM.

nina: LGTM.

tara: will do — follow-up RFC link will be in #architecture when ready.
